clue.text: Fraud stumped group right away

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is sent away, so that letter is dropped from the word before it

blocks.note: st. is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
a ring is a group, as of criminals or dealers

explanation.surface: A con artist's gang is baffled and quits on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: RING loses its R (right) to leave ING after ST. 'Stumped' looks like 'baffled', but it is cricket shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is slang for a confidence trick or swindle, especially an elaborate one.

clue.text: A relation at sea?

blocks.note: surface reading: a family member who is confused, or away on a voyage
setter's reading: a vessel built to the same design as another, so a female relative afloat

explanation.walkthrough: Ships are traditionally 'she', so a vessel of the same class as another is thought of as its female sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel built to the same design as another is called this, ships being female by tradition.

clue.text: Unsuitable home (small apartment)

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
apt. is the short form of apartment

explanation.surface: A tiny flat makes an unsuitable place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means not appropriate or not fitting for the purpose, the opposite of apt.

clue.text: Rule supported by US president, a great help to 11?

blocks.note: government is rule or control of a state
Ulysses S. Grant was the 18th US president

explanation.surface: A policy backed by an American president proves a boon to some project.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'supported by' puts the president underneath. Entry 11 is the enterprise zone, an area funded to attract business.
explanation.definitionFit: State money awarded to boost investment is just what a designated business development area would welcome.

clue.text: Showing agility, I act amazingly after disturbing cobra

indicators.note: disturbing the snake's name jumbles its letters out of their order
done amazingly suggests a surprising transformation, so these letters are rearranged too

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snake charmer, having upset a cobra, performs nimbly to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: the jumbled snake comes first, then 'after' places the jumbled I ACT behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatic describes gymnastic, nimble movement of the kind seen in circus tumbling.

clue.text: Male taken in by various learned former councillors

indicators.note: various suggests different arrangements, so the following word's letters are mixed
something taken in by another goes inside it

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man was welcomed among assorted scholarly town officials of old.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldermen were senior members of English borough and county councils until the office was abolished in 1974, hence 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldermen were senior elected members of a town council, a rank largely abolished in England.

clue.text: Old man tucking into what's left of meal

indicators.note: tucking into something means getting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the rest is what remains
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Dad polishes off the leftovers of dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' suggests eating, which suits the meal picture, but here it means one piece goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal or literary word for a meal or the food eaten at one.

clue.text: One who followed a couple home?

definitions.text: One who followed a couple home?

blocks.clueFragment: One who followed a couple home?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone trailing a pair of people back to their house

blocks.clueFragment: One who followed a couple home?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a competitor who finished just behind two others, crossing the line third

explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' is the finishing line in a race, and 'followed a couple' means came in after two rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The athlete placed third behind gold and silver winners receives the third-place award.

clue.text: Print ad, new one for French cricket?

indicators.note: making something new reshapes the words before it into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
un is the French for one

explanation.surface: An advert for a game, perhaps the children's French cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip-and-run is a casual form of cricket in which the batter must run whenever the ball is hit; 'French cricket' is a decoy, as only 'one for French' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-and-run is an informal version of the bat-and-ball game, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Parish priest in France provides remedy

blocks.note: first meaning: a curé, the French word for a parish priest
second meaning: a treatment that heals

explanation.surface: A French village priest offers a healing treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Accents are ignored in the grid, so the French curé fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a medical treatment that restores health and, accented, the French title for a parish clergyman.

clue.text: Famous victory editor denied?

blocks.note: star used as an adjective, as in a star player
V is the abbreviation for victory
ed. is the short form of editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is refused a celebrated win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Denied?' reads as the editor being refused something, but it is the definition, with the question mark flagging a loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Being starved means being deprived of food or of something needed, such as affection.

clue.text: Succeed the Duke of Milan? Almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the final letter is left off

blocks.note: Prospero, the magician in Shakespeare's The Tempest, is the rightful Duke of Milan

explanation.surface: Someone nearly takes over from the Italian duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' tempts as 'take over from the Duke', but it is the definition meaning thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or do well, which is succeeding in the sense of achieving success.

clue.text: I represent rebuilt end of Suez, one area seeking business investment

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its last letter, which is all we keep

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the canal's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spokesperson for a redeveloped part of Suez promotes it to investors.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise zone is a designated district offering tax breaks and lighter rules to attract new companies.

clue.text: Major 1930s civil engineering work in rock, round the bend coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a boulder is a large rock
round the bend is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A big construction project in stone, built on a curve, rises up.
explanation.walkthrough: Boulder Dam was the original name of the Hoover Dam on the Colorado River, built 1931 to 1936. 'Round the bend' suggests a curve but means insane.
explanation.definitionFit: The great concrete barrier on the Colorado River, finished in 1936, was officially called this before becoming Hoover Dam.

clue.text: Promiscuous woman exposed by Sunday Herald?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
to herald is to trumpet or proclaim, and a herald may blow one

explanation.surface: A scandalous woman is outed by a Sunday newspaper called the Herald.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sunday Herald was a real Scottish paper, so the surface is a tabloid exposé.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumpet is an old-fashioned, disparaging word for a woman regarded as sexually loose or a prostitute.

clue.text: Prompt grabbing a rest

indicators.note: something grabbing another holds it within its grip, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a prompt is a reminder, as to an actor who forgets lines
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cue to take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' tempts as a pause or break, but here it means what is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is the rest, meaning whatever is left over once a part has gone.

clue.text: This could be the beginning or be my undoing

indicators.note: undoing the words takes them apart so their letters can be put back in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something new might be a start, or might ruin me.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is the earliest stage of an organism's development, so figuratively the start of anything.

clue.text: Father's jet is acceptable!

blocks.note: pa is father, with the possessive s
both jet and sable mean intensely black

explanation.surface: Dad's aeroplane will do just fine!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' suggests an aircraft, but it is the colour jet black, and sable is the heraldic word for black.
explanation.definitionFit: Passable means adequate or good enough, which is merely acceptable rather than excellent.

clue.text: Greek character entering foul mine is safe from a particular disease

indicators.note: something entering another goes inside it
foul suggests something fouled up, so the next word's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man going down a filthy pit is protected from infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Being immune means having resistance to an infection, typically through vaccination or past exposure.

clue.text: One may contain greetings in Latin, welcoming in a church dignitary

blocks.note: a birthday or Christmas card carries greetings
taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A greetings card in Latin welcomes a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: The ordering is loose: Latin's abbreviation 'welcomes' the words in and a, which are placed in front of it rather than inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal is a senior Roman Catholic prelate, ranked just below the Pope and one of those electing him.

clue.text: Good drop of red and Asti drunk for free

indicators.note: a drop is the smallest amount, so only the first letter is used
someone drunk is jumbled and unsteady, so the wine's letters are mixed up

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
the opening letter of the word
taken as written; Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A nice splash of red wine and some Asti, consumed at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis is Latin-derived and means without payment, given at no cost.

clue.text: Bugler is so glib after playing for over-sensitive man

indicators.note: after playing about, the words come out in a rearranged form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking trumpeter after a performance mocks a sensitive chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' suits a bugler, but it signals the anagram. Big girl's blouse is British slang for a feeble or oversensitive man.
explanation.definitionFit: Big girl's blouse is a mocking British idiom for a man considered weak, wet or overly emotional.

clue.text: University's wise tradition

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
sage as an adjective means wise

explanation.surface: A university's long-standing custom is a wise one.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established custom or habitual practice, as in language usage handed down over time.

clue.text: One not needed by head cook

indicators.note: something not needed is left out, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a head is a chief or leader

explanation.surface: A kitchen boss doesn't need anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head cook' reads as one phrase, but 'head' is wordplay and 'cook' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook, especially the one in charge of a restaurant kitchen.

clue.text: Unfinished hotel needs worker to find fireplug

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: a hydro is a hotel or spa offering hydropathic treatment
a worker ant, the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A half-built hotel needs a labourer to locate the fire point.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrant is a street water outlet that firefighters connect hoses to, known in America as a fireplug.

clue.text: Bandit has gear in belt

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a band is a belt or strip
rig is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: An outlaw carries his kit tucked into his belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a member of a gang that ambushes and robs travellers, typically in mountains or forests.

clue.text: Rum tot's a free sample

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the following letters are put into an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tot of rum is offered as a free taster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum tot' looks like a measure of spirit, but rum is the British adjective for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample or hint of something to come later.

clue.text: Word describing element of heat?

blocks.note: surface reading: a term for the heating element in a kettle or fire
setter's reading: the word-building element from Greek meaning heat, which is also a unit of heat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' suggests a heating coil, but it is a word element, the Greek-derived root that means heat, as in thermometer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the combining form taken from Greek for warmth and a British unit of heat energy used for gas billing.
